title: Testimony service
hookLine: church members stand and tell what God has done this week

lines: A MAN BY THE LAKE, CLOTHED AND CALM.
cards: A man who lived among the tombs, breaking every chain they put on him and crying out in the hills, is sitting by the lake now, clothed and calm. Mark's Gospel tells it.
Jesus has set him free, and as Jesus climbs back into the boat, the man begs to come along.

Jesus says no: "Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee." So the man goes home and tells it, all over his region. Not a sermon.

teach.h: I WILL DECLARE WHAT HE HATH DONE.
teach.b: A psalm sets the pattern: "Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul." The psalmist doesn't argue. He tells.
In Black churches and Pentecostal churches, the testimony service makes room for exactly that. The floor opens, and one after another, people stand and tell what God has done this week.

teach.h: HONOR TO GOD, THEN THE STORY.
teach.b: Some begin with a familiar opening, giving honor to God, and then the story comes. A job found. A test result.
A son who called after a long silence. A hard week that didn't break them. Sometimes just: I woke up this morning.

And the room answers each one, the way it answered the preacher, with amen and thank you, Jesus. At the center you may hear today's line: God has been good. The Book of Revelation gives testimony real weight.
It says of the faithful: "they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony."
There it's the witness of the faithful under pressure, and some who testify on a Sunday hear their own small reports in that line.

teach.h: A WEEK OF ROOMS WHERE EVERYONE SPEAKS.
teach.b: Today closes a week of rooms: praise with hands raised, a hand on a shoulder and a prayer, a word weighed, bold prayer for the sick, the preacher calling and the people answering, the prayer meeting naming every need, and now the testimony.
In every one, something is said out loud from the pews: a hallelujah, a prayer, a weighed word, an amen, a story.

how: In Black and Pentecostal churches, a part of the service or a midweek meeting is set aside for testimony: members stand, often beginning by giving honor to God, tell what God has done for them, and the congregation responds aloud.

games.q: you've just been set free from what tormented you, and you beg to follow Jesus wherever he goes. what does he tell you?
o: go home and tell your friends what the Lord has done.
games.why: he turns down the request and makes the man a witness at home: "go home to thy friends, and tell them."

practice: Go back through the week a day at a time, last night, the day before, the start of the week, and look for one good thing: a conversation, a meal, a moment you were helped.
When you find it, say it out loud in a sentence or two, plainly, as a report: this happened. If you pray, you can begin it with thanks.

wordCard.voice: Testimony service. A time in worship when members stand and tell, plainly, what God has done for them this week.

orig.note: Greek: testimony, the witness someone bears. The word in Revelation 12:11, the word of their testimony.

carryVoice: Your line: God has been good. Small reports count too, even I woke up this morning. That's the week.
